newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria's Zeroual to hold talks on poll.
newsitem.headline: Algeria's Zeroual to hold talks on poll.

text.p: Algeria's President Liamine Zeroual said on Wednesday he would hold talks with the country's legal opposition on an independent committee to oversee parliamentary elections later this year.

"Consultations with politicians will be engaged soon in order to establish an independent watchdog commission in charge of overseeing the implementation of the election law and to see that the elections are properly taking place in freedom, democracy and tranparency," said Zeroual.

Zeroual, quoted by the official Algerian news agency APS as addressing a cabinet meeting, ordered the government to undertake appropriate measures to install this independent committee and provide all means enabling it to monitor the poll.

"The year 1997 will be the one when all elected institutions will be in place and so the multi-party democracy will be definitely embodied in Algeria," said Zeroual referring to a parliamentary election in the first half of 1997 followed by local polls.
The government has not yet announced official dates for the polls.

Algeria has been without an elected parliament and local councils since January 1992 when the authorities annulled a general election in which radical Islamic Salvation Front (FIS) had taken a commanding lead. The now banned FIS is barred from fielding candidates in the elections.
The cancellation plunged the oil and gas producing country into violence pitting Moslem guerrillas and government forces in which more than 60,000 people have died.
